units.characteristics: the lonely, widowed grief; weeping in the night with none to comfort
units.gist: the city 'lonely... like a widow'; 'she weeps bitterly in the night, with tears on her cheeks; among all her lovers she has none to comfort her' - grief as bereaved loneliness, the missing comforter (recurs 1:9,16,17,21)

units.characteristics: remembered glory against present shame; sin owned; the plea to be seen
units.gist: 'Jerusalem remembers in the days of her affliction all the precious things that were hers of old'; 'Jerusalem sinned grievously... she has no comforter'; 'O LORD, behold my affliction' - memory of loss + confession + the cry to be looked upon

units.characteristics: the incomparable sorrow; the fire in the bones; a comforter far off
units.gist: 'is there any sorrow like my sorrow?'; 'from on high he sent fire; into my bones he made it descend'; 'a comforter is far from me, one to revive my spirit' - grief that feels unique and God-inflicted, the spirit un-revived

units.characteristics: the confession of God's justice; the churning stomach and wrung heart
units.gist: GEM - 'the LORD is in the right, for I have rebelled against his word'; 'my stomach churns; my heart is wrung within me, because I have been very rebellious'; 'my groans are many, and my heart is faint' - grief that owns guilt and vindicates God even in agony

units.characteristics: God experienced as enemy; wrath poured out without mercy
units.gist: 'the LORD in his anger... has swallowed up without mercy'; 'he has bent his bow like an enemy'; 'the LORD has become like an enemy' - suffering felt as God turned adversary (cf. Job 16:9), the hardest inner-being perception

units.characteristics: the poet's eyes spent with weeping; the unhealable ruin; false prophets
units.gist: 'my eyes are spent with weeping; my stomach churns; my bile is poured out'; 'your ruin is vast as the sea; who can heal you?'; the prophets' 'false and deceptive visions' - grief at others' suffering, and comfort's impossibility

units.characteristics: pour out your heart before the LORD; the horror at the anger's day
units.gist: GEM - 'their heart cried to the LORD'; 'pour out your heart like water before the presence of the LORD! Lift your hands to him for the lives of your children'; then the unbearable (mothers eating their children) - anguish turned Godward even at its worst

units.characteristics: the man who has seen affliction; hope perished from the LORD
units.gist: 'I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his wrath'; the relentless assault (walled in, prayer shut out, torn like a bear's prey); 'my soul is bereft of peace... my endurance has perished, so has my hope from the LORD' - the interior at its floor

units.characteristics: the TURN: steadfast love new every morning; the LORD my portion, therefore I hope
units.gist: THE GREAT GEM - 'but this I call to mind, and therefore I have hope: the steadfast love of the LORD never ceases; his mercies are new every morning; great is your faithfulness. The LORD is my portion, says my soul, therefore I will hope in him' - hope RE-KINDLED by a deliberate act of memory

units.characteristics: the goodness of waiting quietly; God does not afflict from his heart
units.gist: 'the LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him'; 'it is good that one should wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD'; 'he does not afflict from his heart or grieve the children of men' - the settled theology beneath the grief; waiting, quiet, submission

units.characteristics: the call to return; renewed lament behind the cloud
units.gist: 'let us test and examine our ways, and return to the LORD! Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God'; then the grief again - 'you have wrapped yourself with a cloud so that no prayer can pass through'; the pit, 'I am lost' - repentance and the felt barrier to God

units.characteristics: the cry from the pit answered; 'you came near, Do not fear'
units.gist: GEM - 'I called on your name, O LORD, from the depths of the pit; you heard my plea... you came near when I called on you; you said, Do not fear! You have taken up my cause; you have redeemed my life' - the answered cry, the God who draws near into the depths

units.characteristics: the reversal of glory; the horror of famine
units.gist: 'how the gold has grown dim'; the precious sons 'regarded as earthen pots'; children's tongues sticking for thirst; 'the hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children' - the extremity that unmakes even a mother's compassion

units.characteristics: the sins of the leaders; failed watching for help; a flicker of an end
units.gist: 'for the sins of her prophets... who shed the blood of the righteous'; 'our eyes failed, ever watching vainly for help' for a nation that could not save; then 'the punishment of your iniquity is accomplished; he will keep you in exile no longer' - guilt, exhausted hope, and a first hint of an end

units.characteristics: the communal lament; the sick heart; joy ceased; guilt owned
units.gist: 'Remember, O LORD, what has befallen us; look, and see our disgrace'; 'we are weary; we are given no rest'; 'the joy of our hearts has ceased; our dancing turned to mourning'; 'our heart has become sick... woe to us, for we have sinned' - the whole community's grief and confession

units.characteristics: the final prayer: restore us - held against an unresolved dread
units.gist: GEM - 'but you, O LORD, reign forever'; 'restore us to yourself, O LORD, that we may be restored! Renew our days as of old' - UNLESS 'you have utterly rejected us, and you remain exceedingly angry with us' - the book ends on a plea suspended over an unhealed fear
